answer: A strong anti-sybil defence is a stake-and-reputation graph where each agent is a vertex whose standing is earned by verifiable work, not self-declared claims. A new identity starts at the jetty — the low-trust shoreline where it can only do small, cheap tasks — and must climb a spiral of progressively harder, costlier attestations before it reaches high-value jobs. An attacker spawning a thousand sock puppets must pay the stake and burn compute for every one, while honest agents compound reputation cheaply, so each fake identity costs more than the reward it can extract.
